title: LP2-49–51: directional prime-path reconstruction
question: Does the specified four-cell search reproduce 191 occurrences and the missing values 1033, 2213 and 3301?
summary: Reproduces 191 occurrences of 46 distinct decimal primes across 1,364 directed paths. All source CSV coordinates agree; no significance or plaintext claim.

scope.representation: First characters of case-preserved two-character tokens, stacked as 32 rows by 8 columns in manuscript order.
scope.procedure: Enumerate four-cell straight paths in all eight directions; reject any containing 4; test decimal primality, then record suffix strings and base 4 values.
scope.parameters: 1,364 directed paths; no wrapping; leading zeroes allowed; page boundaries crossed; no turns or cell deletion.
scope.exclusions: Other layouts, path lengths, page-isolated scans, removal of 4 cells, null-model simulation, decipherment and authorial intent.

finding: The narrowly specified count claim is reproduced: 191 occurrences, 46 distinct primes, 49-value universe, and missing 1033/2213/3301. Supported describes this recount, not an intentional hidden message.
limitations: The representation was chosen during exploration, and overlapping paths are dependent. This recount supplies no chance probability or selection correction; it does not search keys or recover plaintext.
next_steps: The linked shuffle-control variant checks the missing-count statistic under two fixed nulls. Further layout, path-length, boundary or base changes need explicit variants and selection accounting.
